description: Three jointed arms turning at their own speeds, in 6HP, their end point read out as an X and a Y voltage

params.text: Sets how fast that arm turns and in which direction, up to 50 turns a second either way, and motionless at the centre
Attenuates and inverts that arm's rotation CV between -100% and +100%, and comes up at 0%
Sets how long that arm is; the three lengths matter only against each other, and an arm at zero drops out
Attenuates and inverts that arm's length CV between -100% and +100%, and comes up at 0%
Sets how wide a span the X and Y outputs cover, 0V to 10V
Attenuates and inverts the range CV between -100% and +100%, and comes up at 0%
Sets where the span falls, -10V to +10V, read as its bottom, middle or top according to the button beside it
Attenuates and inverts the anchor CV between -100% and +100%, and comes up at 0%
Steps the anchor knob's meaning through minimum, centre and maximum, with a light showing which

inputs.text: Moves that arm's turning speed, 5V covering half the knob's travel at full trim
Moves that arm's length, 10V covering the knob's full travel at full trim
Adds its voltage to the range after the trim knob
Adds its voltage to the anchor after the trim knob

outputs.text: Carries the horizontal position of the third arm's end point, scaled into the chosen span
Carries the vertical position of the third arm's end point, scaled into the chosen span
Carries the X and Y outputs added together and halved

notes: with the second and third arms at zero length the first arm alone turns, and X and Y become a sine and a cosine at its speed
with fixed lengths and speeds the pattern repeats; the chaos settings on the menu, or CV into the arm controls, are what stop it repeating
this module is monophonic, and a small drawing at the bottom left shows the three arms as they move
menu: Rot.vel. scale-mode: Exp, Linear, Log — bends how the rotation knobs respond across their travel, with a light beside the label green for Exp and red for Log
Arm-1 rot. chaos, Arm-2 rot. chaos, Arm-3 rot. chaos — picks a new speed factor for that arm each time it passes zero degrees, in steps of 5% up to 100%
Arm-1 length chaos, Arm-2 length chaos, Arm-3 length chaos — picks a new length factor for that arm each time it passes zero degrees, faded in and out over the turn so the curves stay smooth
Clipping range — clamps every output to the range chosen, -12V to 12V unless you change it, and Off lets the output run to any voltage
Process quality: Audio, High, Balanced, Low, Very low — sets how often the module runs its algorithm, from every cycle down to every 256th; below Balanced a 1ms trigger can be missed
Auto select process quality — picks the process quality from the dialled-in rate and from which ports are patched, and greys out the manual choice while it is on
